title: feat(app-showcase): expand page-capability coverage (visualizations, config depth, record components)
body:
## Summary

Rounds out the showcase so it demonstrates the **full page surface**, not just a couple of grid interface pages. Answers "what's the most complete way to show off page capabilities".

### P1 — every record visualization as its own interface page
`task-visualizations.pages.ts`: **Task Board** (kanban) · **Task Calendar** · **Task Gallery** · **Team Schedule** (gantt) · **Activity Timeline** · **Work Map** · **All Views** (one page whose switcher spans all 7). Each whitelists one visualization and relies on runtime auto-derive for the bindings; each page's `columns` include the binding fields so the data is actually fetched.

### P2 — deeper interface config
`active-projects.page.ts`: `filterBy` always-on base filter (hide completed) · default `sort` (budget desc) · `addRecord` toolbar **form** entry point · dropdown user-filters · grid+kanban.

### P3 — record-layout component set
`task-detail.page.ts` (full record page): `record:path` status stepper · `record:alert` with a `visible` expression (shows only In Review) · `record:quick_actions` (object actions) · highlights · details.

### P4 — data
Cover images on tasks (gallery), reusing the existing lat/lng locations (map).

## Verification (browser, live showcase)
- All 7 visualization pages render — **Work Map** shows 10 pins, **Task Gallery** 10 covers, **Team Schedule** gantt bars, plus calendar/timeline/kanban; **All Views** switcher offers all 7.
- **Active Projects** hides the completed project (filterBy) and sorts by budget desc.
- **Task** record page shows the path stepper (Backlog→…→Done), the In-Review alert, and quick actions.

## Deferred (follow-up — heavier/uncertain renderers)
- Hierarchy `levels` (needs a self-referencing object + tree renderer).
- A `utility`-type panel page.

Pairs with objectstack-ai/objectui#1811 (gantt/map auto-derive).
